title.narrative: Sustainable Supplier Development Programme (SSDP): a public-private partnership to increase safe and sustainable sourcing and business linkages between suppliers in Malaysia and Japanese retailers

description.narrative: Small suppliers in Malaysia face difficulties to respond to the demand of the markets in terms of quality, quantity, productivity and sustainability leading to inability to tap the opportunity of trading with major local/regional/global buyers/retailers. Developing the supply-side through clustering and upgrading of MSMEs would entail networking and collective and individual actions to improve management, quality, safety, production and sustainability practices with an impact on their overall business and social performance and reliability. Special attention will be given to integrating business objectives with sustainable social development at enterprise, cluster and country level. Based on request of AEON and the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, MOFA, UNIDO will implement a Sustainable Supplier Development Programme in Malaysia, which follows the same approach implemented by UNIDO with METRO in Egypt, Russia and India. The project will initiate with AEON current and potential suppliers in Malaysia and based on the result of the project, expansion to other countries in the region and other retailers and sectors is considered.
